summary: DistKvCacheEvent declares group_idx default null; a BlockStored without group_idx goes through kv-event-aggregator and comes back with group_idx null (kv_events.py:82). Only a struct default, so the evidence is schema-level.

With ExampleConnector, 3x48-token requests get 3 block hashes each; scheduler.schedule calls kv-connector-base-v1.build-connector-meta with every new request's block ids equal to scheduled_new_reqs, attaches kv_connector_metadata and leaves no kv_connector_block_state (scheduler.py:1459-1547). The plugin that overrides Scheduler._build_kv_connector_meta and the DummyKVConnector are test code (untranslatable part). Note: the model passes scheduled_new_reqs, not a KVConnectorBlockState over all scheduled requests incl. cached ones (scheduler.py:1464-1472); the test does not exercise that difference.

The assertion is on generated text from MyOPTForCausalLM.compute_logits zeroing logits (tests/plugins/vllm_add_dummy_model/my_opt.py), below the model. Registry part passes: register-model then resolve-model-cls resolves MyOPTForCausalLM. Side finding (config-platform): plugins.load-general-plugins only targets the filesystem/HF-hub resolvers and calls targets with no input, so a general plugin that calls ModelRegistry.register_model (the test's real path) can't be expressed.

With distributed-executor-backend external_launcher on TP>1, startup fails: the model runs UniProcExecutor's single rank0 worker, so the profile run's TP all-reduce waits for ranks that never run and fails dist-backend-error after 600 s. Code: ExecutorWithExternalLauncher (vllm/v1/executor/uniproc_executor.py:161-207) is one engine per torchrun rank, and determine_available_memory all-reduces the budget with ReduceOp.MIN over the world CPU group so every rank sizes the same KV cache; neither the per-rank engines nor the MIN all-reduce is modeled.
